commands.command: Implement repopact-mobile-saf (the Android SAF plugin crate)
commands.summary: New workspace crate. Cargo.toml: build-dependency tauri-plugin 2.6.3 (features=['build'], matching the vendored dialog plugin's exact spec after discovering the default 'runtime'-only feature set does not expose Builder), dependency on tauri 2.11.5 and repopact-mobile-acquisition. build.rs: tauri_plugin::Builder::new(&[]).android_path('android').try_build() -- an empty COMMANDS list because this crate deliberately exposes no frontend-invokable commands of its own (WI065 Checkpoint B §6: no read_uri/list_uri/write_uri surface reachable from JS). src/lib.rs: SafAcquisitionExt<R> blanket trait giving any Manager<R> a .saf_acquisition() accessor; SafAcquisition<R> wraps a PluginHandle<R> on mobile and a Send+Sync PhantomData<fn() -> R> stub on desktop (SAF has no desktop equivalent; the type exists only so the crate compiles under a plain host cargo check). src/mobile.rs: pick_directory_tree/pick_archive_document (blocking run_mobile_plugin calls returning Option<Picked*>, None on user cancellation -- not an error), a Kotlin-failure-reason-to-ErrorCode mapping, AndroidSafSource (implements repopact_mobile_acquisition::source::AcquisitionSource by lazily calling 'listChildren' once per directory actually visited -- never a single upfront tree walk), and open_document_to_staging/StagingFile/StagingArchiveFile (copy a picked document into an app-private staging file via the 'openDocument' plugin command, then read it back with an ordinary std::fs::File; the staging file self-deletes on Drop).

Recorded directly in mobile.rs's doc comments: Tauri's mobile-plugin invoke channel in this version is JSON-in/JSON-out (PluginHandle::run_mobile_plugin<T: DeserializeOwned>) with no supported live-stream/fd handoff; base64-through-JSON and a custom chunked-pull protocol were both rejected (memory-doubling and per-file round-trip complexity respectively); a native, app-private (Android cacheDir-rooted) staging file is the narrowest mechanism that keeps actual byte content off the JSON channel entirely, with Checkpoint A's own bounded-copy loop remaining the true resource-accounting authority regardless of what the staging copy's own generous safety-net cap allowed through.

rust/crates/repopact-mobile-saf/android/: build.gradle.kts (namespace com.forgewirelabs.repopact.mobileacquisition, mirrors tauri-plugin-dialog's android/build.gradle.kts exactly, including implementation(project(':tauri-android'))), an empty AndroidManifest.xml (SAF requires no manifest permission), consumer-rules.pro, and src/main/java/.../SafAcquisitionPlugin.kt implementing pickDirectoryTree (Intent.ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT_TREE via startActivityForResult/@ActivityCallback, distinguishing RESULT_CANCELED (returns {status:'cancelled'}, not an error) from RESULT_OK/other, calling contentResolver.takePersistableUriPermission(uri, FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION) wrapped in try/catch for providers that refuse persistable grants -- logged, never escalated to broader storage permission), pickArchiveDocument (Intent.ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT + CATEGORY_OPENABLE + a ZIP-ish MIME filter for UX only, no persistable grant requested since archive picks are one-shot), listChildren (DocumentsContract.buildChildDocumentsUriUsingTree + a bounded ContentResolver.query per directory, mapping a missing/null document id or display name to a typed provider_failure/unsupported_entry outcome rather than defaulting or crashing), and openDocument (ContentResolver.openInputStream copied into an app-private cacheDir/saf-stage/<uuid>.bin file under a generous byte-cap safety net, never the resource-accounting authority).

commands.command: Fix a real XML-comment defect found by the first real Gradle build attempt
commands.summary: The plugin's first AndroidManifest.xml contained a `--` sequence inside an XML comment (illegal per the XML spec, though many lenient parsers tolerate it); Android's manifmerger.ManifestMerger2 does not, and the first `tauri android build` run failed at :repopact-mobile-saf:processDebugManifest with a MergeFailureException. Fixed by rewording the comment to avoid `--`; documented here rather than silently patched without record, since it is a real, reproducible defect this checkpoint's own real-build attempt surfaced (WI065 Checkpoint B's own instruction not to fabricate build success -- this was a genuine failure, genuinely fixed, then genuinely re-verified).

New module. MobileAcquisitionCoordinator wraps one WorkspaceManager (Decision 0057's own crash/restart recovery runs exactly once, in run()'s setup closure, rooted at app.path().app_data_dir()?.join('repositories') -- never WI060's debug validation path) plus an operations: Mutex<HashMap<String, OperationEntry>> for the frontend-facing operation-id/progress/cancellation-token bookkeeping Checkpoint A's WorkspaceManager itself does not expose externally. Typed commands: mobile_workspace_list, mobile_git_capabilities, mobile_operation_status, mobile_operation_cancel, mobile_workspace_open (resolves a workspace id to its app-private repository PathBuf through the registry, then calls the existing, unmodified DesktopService::open_repository -- never accepts a caller-provided path), mobile_import_directory, mobile_import_archive (both: pick via the SAF bridge, which blocks on user interaction exactly like desktop's select_repository already blocks on its native folder dialog; on selection, register an operation id/CancellationToken pair and spawn a background thread that drives Checkpoint A's existing import_directory/import_archive against an AndroidSafSource/staged archive file, updating the coordinator's progress map via the existing ProgressThrottle-throttled callback; on cancellation/completion, the coordinator records the exact terminal state -- Succeeded/Failed/Cancelled -- Checkpoint A's own AcquisitionError::code already distinguishes). No read_uri/write_uri/list_uri/arbitrary-path/generic-shell command exists anywhere in this surface.

select_repository is unchanged and remains desktop-only in behavior; run()'s invoke_handler is now fully platform-branched (not just the plugin list) -- the non-Android build's generate_handler! list is exactly the pre-Checkpoint-B command set, and the Android build's list additionally includes the seven mobile_* commands. MobileAcquisitionCoordinator and every command except mobile_import_directory/mobile_import_archive compile and host-test on every platform (only the two import commands, which call the real SAF bridge, are #[cfg(target_os = 'android')]-gated) -- but only the Android build's invoke_handler ever registers any of them, so desktop's command surface is unaffected either way.

permissions/workbench.toml's commands.allow gained the seven mobile_* command names (no new permission identifier, no broadened scope) -- gen/schemas/acl-manifests.json regenerated accordingly and confirmed to show only that addition via git diff.
